summary: Okanogan National Forest 20-foot L-4 pole tower built 1935 on Pearygin Peak; removed or destroyed in 1953; a 2022 visitor found an outhouse and relic wood on the summit.

access.note: On Okanogan National Forest land; the 2022 visitor account describes a hike and mentions no closure or gate. Inferred from that account, not a posted status

visit.trail_note: About 3 miles one way with 2,000 feet of gain. The road is washed out about half a mile short of the end, and the last mile and a half is a rough bushwhack (2022 account)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Willhite give 20 feet for the 1935 tower. Willhite's quotation of a 1950 USGS description gives a wooden building about 40 feet high. The story reports both and does not choose.
The register says removed in 1953; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed in 1953. The year agrees across sources, so the event is recorded as destroyed with the register's wording noted.

notes_for_editor: Spelling: the register and Forest Lookouts use Pearygin; Willhite uses Pearrygin. The record keeps Pearygin. The only account of the site today is one 2022 visit on WillhiteWeb, and the access level 'public' is inferred from National Forest land and that account. The Okanogan County Historical Society photo record returned HTTP 403, so it was not read. No staffing or fire records were found in these four sources.
